This is direct, locally specific evidence of how the national Pride-ban policy was enforced here, the key factual basis for this record's risk assessment.

It records the escalating police suppression with numbers: blockades and tear gas in 2021 with 25 arrested; 373 arrested in 2022 with public transport to the central square shut down; 113 arrests in 2023; and 11 arrests in 2024 (three of them minors) after organisers moved the event to other public spaces and issued fake meeting calls to thwart police. This frames the record's 'banned for a ninth consecutive year' claim with a per-year detention tally a visitor can weigh.

An English-language news outlet (27 June 2022) reports that on 26 June 2022 riot police dispersed the Pride march in this city's central square, blockaded streets in a nearby neighbourhood, shut down public transport to the square, and detained 373 people — including an international press photographer — who were released after a night in custody, according to the country's leading LGBTI rights organisation. The district governors' offices had banned all LGBTI+ Pride Week events for seven days, and eight more people were detained at a Pride march in another city. The piece reports Pride has been banned by the country's authorities since 2014 and that police crackdowns on the parades have grown harsher over the years.
